domains.name: Strategic Crew Heist
domains.promise: A guild crew pulls off strategic play-money heists: any member spends play-money coins to /heist start a job against a randomly chosen target, teammates /heist join within the recruiting window — each freezing the exact entry fee they paid on their own economy_heist_participants row — and once the window closes the claimed crew shares one frozen outcome. A success pays every frozen crew member the frozen per-person payout_each exactly once, a failure forfeits their entry fees, and an under-crewed or cancelled job refunds each participant their own frozen entry_fee_paid; late joins that never made the frozen crew are reconciled and refunded rather than dragged into the outcome. Every coin is play-money inside the fake game economy — never real commerce, never a market-sellable asset, and a commerce-held role earns no heist income — and money plus heist state stay idempotent under replay, crash, and concurrent join or resolve.

controls.description: Master switch for heists (config key economy_heist_enabled); when off, /heist commands explain the feature is disabled and no heist can start or resolve.
Play-money coin cost each member pays to /heist start or /heist join (config key economy_heist_entry_fee); frozen per participant as entry_fee_paid at join time.
Base play-money coin payout (config key economy_heist_base_payout) scaled by the randomly chosen target's payout modifier and split among the crew on success.
Single-member base success percentage (config key economy_heist_success_base_pct); the derived chance is base plus target difficulty modifier plus 7 per extra crew member, capped at 95.
Seconds the recruiting window stays open for /heist join before the heist is claimed and resolved (config key economy_heist_join_window_secs).
Seconds a guild must wait after a heist resolves before another /heist start is allowed (config key economy_heist_cooldown_seconds).
Minimum crew size required for a heist to attempt resolution (config key economy_heist_min_participants); below this the heist cancels and refunds every entry fee.
Maximum crew size a single heist admits (config key economy_heist_max_participants); further /heist join attempts are refused as crew-full.

defaults.rationale: Crew heists are a flagship social game-economy loop and ship on for the maximal out-of-box experience; the stakes stay real-but-recoverable because every fee is refunded on any non-failure outcome.

A conservative, fully configurable wager that makes joining a deliberate choice without punishing casual players, and is frozen per member so a mid-window edit never changes what anyone already risked.
A meaningful play-coin reward the target modifier scales from, giving a quick early win for a small crew and a long-term chase on the hardest targets.
A balanced solo baseline: risky alone, clearly better with a bigger crew, so recruiting always feels worthwhile while staying a conservative bet.
A minute is long enough for a guild to rally a crew and short enough to keep the tension of a live heist.
A five-minute lull keeps heists a special event rather than a coin faucet, protecting the play-money economy from grind spam.
A heist is a crew activity; requiring at least two keeps it cooperative, and anything short of the minimum refunds everyone rather than gambling a lone member.
Eight is a lively crew ceiling that keeps per-person payouts meaningful; owners can widen or narrow it freely.

permissions.enforcement: Heist slash commands respond for every member; heist_start and heist_join debit and freeze the entry fee on the invoking member's own participant row, and no command lets a member act on another member's wallet or crew slot.

permissions.actor: Dashboard user with owner or admin access to the guild
permissions.action: Edit heist settings on the dashboard economy heist page
permissions.enforcement: Dashboard session auth plus Supabase RLS restrict guild_config writes to authorized guild administrators.

permissions.action: Redirect, double-claim, or collect another crew member's frozen payout or refund
permissions.enforcement: heist_credit_participant is keyed to each participant's own heist and user id under the paid_at guard, and every refund reads that row's own frozen entry_fee_paid; no code path pays one member's share to another wallet.

messages.trigger: A member starts a heist with /heist start and pays the entry fee
messages.defaultTemplate: {initiator-name} is assembling a crew to hit {target-name} for up to {payout} play coins — join for {entry-fee}, base odds {base-chance}%. Use /heist join within {join-window} seconds!

messages.trigger: A member joins the recruiting crew with /heist join
messages.audience: The joining member and the channel
messages.defaultTemplate: {member-name} joined the crew as the {role}! The crew is now {crew-size} strong with {success-chance}% success odds.

messages.trigger: A heist resolves as a success
messages.defaultTemplate: Heist success at {target-name}! Each of the {crew-size} crew members pockets {payout-each} play coins.

messages.trigger: A heist resolves as a failure
messages.defaultTemplate: The heist on {target-name} fell apart — every crew member forfeits their {entry-fee} play-coin entry fee.

messages.trigger: The join window closes with fewer than the minimum crew members
messages.defaultTemplate: Heist cancelled — only {crew-size} joined but {min-crew} were needed. Every entry fee has been refunded.

messages.trigger: The entry fee was debited but the atomic heist_start insert failed
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the invoking member
messages.defaultTemplate: That heist never got off the ground, {member-name} — your {entry-fee} play coins are already back in your wallet.

messages.trigger: The heist backend is temporarily unreachable when a member runs a heist command
messages.surface: Ephemeral reply to the invoking member
messages.defaultTemplate: The crew's comms are down, {member-name} — give it a moment and try /heist again.

messages.trigger: One or more crew payouts or refunds keep failing after a heist is resolved
messages.defaultTemplate: Heads up: {failed-count} heist payout(s) on {target-name} failed and are queued for automatic retry; nothing was double-paid and every frozen amount is logged.

values.description: No active heist for this guild; /heist start can begin one once the cooldown has elapsed, and /heist status shows the last resolved heist.
A heist is open; members join with /heist join within the window, each atomically debited and freezing their own entry_fee_paid on a participant row.
The window closed and heist_claim_for_resolution atomically flipped recruiting to in_progress, freezing the outcome and payout_each on the row; payouts and refunds settle idempotently.
The heist resolved as a success; every frozen crew member was credited their frozen payout_each exactly once and the row was finalized once.
The heist resolved as a failure; every crew member forfeited their entry fee, nothing was credited, and the row was finalized once.
The window closed below the minimum crew; every participant was refunded their own frozen entry_fee_paid exactly once before the row was finalized.
Heists disabled by configuration; /heist commands explain the feature is off and no heist can start or resolve.

transitions.trigger: A member runs /heist start with sufficient play-money balance and the cooldown elapsed
transitions.expectedEffect: heist_start atomically debits exactly one entry fee and creates the heist plus the initiator participant row (freezing entry_fee_paid) in one transaction, then the recruiting embed posts.

transitions.trigger: A member runs /heist join inside the window
transitions.expectedEffect: heist_join re-checks recruiting under the heist-row lock, debits and freezes the member's own entry_fee_paid, inserts one participant row, and derives the new success chance from the participant-row count — no fee is charged if the claim already won the lock.

transitions.trigger: The join window expires and a single resolver claims the heist
transitions.expectedEffect: heist_claim_for_resolution flips recruiting to in_progress under FOR UPDATE for exactly one caller, freezing the outcome and payout_each and stamping claimed_at on the crew set.

transitions.trigger: The frozen outcome is success and every credit settles
transitions.expectedEffect: heist_credit_participant pays each frozen crew member payout_each idempotently under the paid_at guard, then heist_finalize_resolution performs the single terminal flip and the success embed announces once.
No credits are made, heist_finalize_resolution performs the single terminal flip, and the failure embed announces the forfeited entry fees once.

transitions.trigger: The claimed crew is below economy_heist_min_participants
transitions.expectedEffect: Each frozen participant is refunded their own entry_fee_paid idempotently under the paid_at guard, then heist_finalize_resolution flips the row terminal once and the cancellation embed announces the refunds.

transitions.trigger: Owner turns economy_heist_enabled off on the dashboard
transitions.expectedEffect: New /heist commands reply with the disabled explanation; existing heist and participant rows are preserved untouched.
Heists can start again on the configured cooldown with all prior heist history intact.

failures.trigger: The entry fee debit succeeds but the atomic heist_start insert fails or a concurrent start already holds the active-heist slot
failures.expectedBehavior: The debited entry fee is refunded exactly once through economy_add_balance, the initiator sees the refund confirmation, and no orphan heist or participant row exists.

failures.trigger: One or more heist_credit_participant calls fail while paying a success or refunding a cancellation
failures.expectedBehavior: The heist stays in_progress with its frozen decision and payout_each; unpaid rows keep paid_at NULL and are flagged payout_failed, a bounded in-process retry (then resumePendingHeists on restart) settles only the still-unpaid members, already-paid crew are never double-credited, and the resolution is not announced until every credit lands.

failures.trigger: heist_claim_for_resolution hits a transient error at the join-window expiry
failures.expectedBehavior: No outcome is ever guessed; the row is left recruiting-and-expired and a bounded in-process retry re-enters resolution so the guild is not blocked, and the heist is still claimed exactly once when the retry succeeds.
